questions.question: Name the organism for each scenario: AML patient with a line and bullous skin lesions and gram-positive bacilli; BMT patient on ciprofloxacin prophylaxis with gram-positive cocci in chains; AML patient with gram-positive bacilli meningitis.
questions.question_raw: Name the bug: AML with line and bullous skin lesions with GPB; BMT patient on cipro prophylaxis with GPC in chains; AML patient with GPB meningitis

parts.text: AML with a line and bullous skin lesions with gram-positive bacilli.
BMT patient on ciprofloxacin prophylaxis with gram-positive cocci in chains.
AML patient with gram-positive bacilli meningitis.

parts_raw.text: AML with line and bullous skin lesions with GPB
BMT patient on cipro prophylaxis with GPC in chains

questions.model_answer: a) Clostridium septicum (gas-forming, associated with neutropenic enterocolitis and bullous/necrotic lesions; consider Bacillus cereus for line-associated bullous disease in AML). b) Viridans-group streptococci (e.g. Streptococcus mitis), which survive on damaged mucosa despite fluoroquinolone prophylaxis. c) Listeria monocytogenes.
questions.beyond_mandell: C. septicum (neutropenic enterocolitis/clostridial sepsis) and viridans streptococci on quinolone prophylaxis are grounded in Ch. 305 (pp. 3623-3625); Listeria as the gram-positive-bacillus meningitis pathogen is standard ID knowledge (Listeria is noted only in the iron-overload context in this chapter).

cohort_answer.text: AML with bullous skin/GPB: Clostridium septicum. BMT on cipro with GPC chains: viridans group Streptococcus / Enterococcus spp. AML with GPB meningitis: Listeria monocytogenes.
